metadata.title: fix(product): Support non-Latin characters in product handles with Un…

issue_payload.body:
# Summary (final PR implementation)

**What** — What changes are introduced in this PR?

This PR fixes and closes issue #14378: products with non-Latin titles (Persian, Arabic, Japanese, Chinese, Korean, Russian, etc.) cannot be created because handle generation fails.

**Three specific changes:**

1. **Improve `toHandle()`** to preserve Unicode letters from any language while still removing special characters (apostrophes, punctuation, etc.)
2. **Update `isValidHandle()`** to be Unicode-aware with proper lowercase validation
3. **Add comprehensive tests** for all scripts and edge cases

**Why** — Why are these changes relevant or necessary?  

Currently, products with non-Latin titles (Persian, Arabic, Japanese, Chinese, Korean, Russian, etc.) cannot be created. The error message is:
```
Invalid product handle '-'. It must contain URL safe characters
```

Root cause: `toHandle()` was stripping all non-ASCII characters, resulting in empty or partial handles.

**How** — How have these changes been implemented?

**Change 1: Improve `toHandle()` in `to-handle.ts`**
- Preserves Unicode letters (`\p{L}`) and numbers (`\p{N}`)
- Removes special characters (apostrophes, punctuation, symbols)
- Replaces spaces/underscores with hyphens
- Falls back to random suffix for empty results

**Change 2: Update `isValidHandle()` in `is-valid-handle.ts`**
- Rejects uppercase ASCII letters (maintains backward compatibility)
- Accepts lowercase letters + case-less scripts (Arabic, Persian, CJK)
- Validates format (no spaces, no special chars, valid hyphen placement)

***Note: No change to product module*** - continues using `toHandle()`


**Testing** — How have these changes been tested, or how can the reviewer test the feature?

- Added unit tests for 10+ language scripts (Persian, Arabic, Japanese, Chinese, Korean, Russian, English)
- Added edge case tests (empty strings, special characters only, accents)
- Verified backward compatibility (Latin handles unchanged)
- Verified categories/collections unchanged

---

## Examples

```typescript
// Persian
toHandle("کتاب فارسی") // "کتاب-فارسی"

// Accents preserved
toHandle("café") // "café"

// Special characters removed
toHandle("Women's Shoes") // "womens-shoes"

// Edge case fallback
toHandle("") // "product-abc123" (random, unique)

// Validation
isValidHandle("کتاب-فارسی") // true
isValidHandle("Hello-World") // false (uppercase rejected)
```

---

## Checklist

Please ensure the following before requesting a review:

- [x] I have added a **changeset** for this PR
- [x] The changes are covered by relevant **tests**
- [x] I have verified the code works as intended locally
- [x] Verified backwards compatibility
- [x] I have linked the related issue(s) if applicable

---

## Additional Context

Closes #14378

This approach follows the established pattern of major ecommerce platforms:

| Platform | Slug/Handle Approach | Unicode Support |
|----------|---------------------|-----------------|
| **WordPress** | `sanitize_title()` – preserves Unicode | ✅ Yes |
| **WooCommerce** | UTF-8 in product permalinks | ✅ Yes |
| **Shopify** | Transliterates to Latin or preserves Unicode | ✅ Yes |
| **Shopware** | Full Unicode slug support | ✅ Yes |
| **Medusa (Current)** | Latin-only + stripping | ❌ No |
| **Medusa (This PR)** | Unicode-aware + `kebabCase` | ✅ Yes |

discussion_timeline.author: medusa-os-bot[bot]
discussion_timeline.body:
Thank you for your contribution, @Cpidar\!

After reviewing this PR, we need a few things addressed before we can move forward:

**Required changes:**
- [ ] Fix the changeset message format in `.changeset/fix-product-handle-unicode.md` — the message must follow the pattern `fix(package-name1, package-name2): description`. Update it to: `fix(product, utils): Support non-Latin characters in product handles`
- [ ] Update the existing test file `packages/core/utils/src/common/__tests__/is-valid-handle.spec.ts` to cover the new Unicode behavior (Persian, Arabic, Japanese, etc.) and protect against regressions. The test file already exists but is not included in this PR.
- [ ] Address the unintended acceptance of uppercase Latin handles introduced by the regex change (see Potential Bugs below)

**Potential Bugs:**

⚠️ `packages/core/utils/src/common/validate-handle.ts` — Regex change unintentionally accepts uppercase Latin handles
```typescript
return /^[\p{L}\p{N}]+(?:-[\p{L}\p{N}]+)*$/u.test(value)
```
The old regex `[a-z0-9]` only matched lowercase letters. The Unicode category `\p{L}` includes *all* letters — uppercase and lowercase alike (`\p{Lu}` + `\p{Ll}` + others). This means `isValidHandle("MyProduct")` now returns `true` where it previously returned `false`. Since product handles are URL slugs that have historically been lowercase-only, this is a silent behavioral regression. Consider one of these fixes:
1. Normalize the value to lowercase before validating: `value.toLowerCase()` (safe for ASCII/Cyrillic/Greek; no-op for caseless scripts like Arabic and CJK)
2. Restrict to `[\p{Ll}\p{Lo}\p{N}]` — lowercase letters (`\p{Ll}`), letters with no case distinction (`\p{Lo}`, which covers Arabic, Hebrew, CJK, Devanagari, etc.), and numbers

**Notes:**
- Both `packages/core/utils/src/common/validate-handle.ts` and `.changeset/fix-product-handle-unicode.md` are missing a trailing newline at end of file.

_Triggered by: new PR opened_

discussion_timeline.author: medusa-os-bot[bot]
discussion_timeline.body:
Thank you for your contribution, @Cpidar\!

Progress from the previous review — all three required changes have been addressed:
- ✅ Changeset message format corrected to `fix(product, utils): Support non-Latin characters in product handles`
- ✅ `is-valid-handle.spec.ts` updated with comprehensive Unicode test coverage (Persian, Arabic, Hebrew, Japanese, Chinese, Korean, Russian, Greek, and edge cases)
- ✅ Uppercase Latin regression addressed via `.toLowerCase()` normalization before the regex test

However, there is a new issue introduced in this commit that needs to be fixed before we can move forward:

**Required changes:**
- [ ] Fix product handle auto-generation to use the new Unicode-aware `toHandle` instead of `kebabCase` — see Potential Bugs below

**Potential Bugs:**

⚠️ `packages/modules/product/src/services/product-module-service.ts` — `kebabCase` doesn't strip special characters, producing invalid stored handles

```typescript
productData.handle = kebabCase(productData.title)
```

`kebabCase` only converts camelCase transitions and spaces/underscores to hyphens — it does **not** remove special characters like `%`, `.`, `\!`, `@`, etc. This introduces a regression for product titles that previously worked:

- `"25% OFF"` → `kebabCase` → `"25%-off"` → stored as an invalid handle (`%` is not allowed)
- `"user.product"` → `kebabCase` → `"user.product"` → stored as an invalid handle (`.` is not allowed)

The old `toHandle` stripped these characters. The **new Unicode-aware `toHandle`** from this same PR (`to-handle.ts`) also handles them correctly via `.replace(/[^\p{L}\p{N}\s_-]/gu, '')`. The fix is to keep using `toHandle` in the product module service and restore the import:

```typescript
// Keep the toHandle import and use it — the rewritten toHandle in this PR
// handles both Unicode titles and special-character titles correctly
productData.handle = toHandle(productData.title)
```

With the rewritten `toHandle`, `"کتاب فارسی"` → `"کتاب-فارسی"` ✅ and `"25% OFF"` → `"25-off"` ✅.

**Notes:**
- `packages/core/utils/src/common/validate-handle.ts` and `packages/core/utils/src/common/__tests__/is-valid-handle.spec.ts` are both still missing a trailing newline at end of file (carried over from the previous review note).
- The `"should validate cleaned handles"` `it` block in `to-handle.spec.ts` has its body indented at 2 spaces rather than 4 — minor style issue.

_Triggered by: new commit pushed_

@medusa-os-bot Thank you for the feedback! I've addressed all issues:

✅ **Changeset format fixed** - Updated to `fix(product, utils): Support non-Latin characters in product handles`

✅ **Tests added** - Created comprehensive tests for both `toHandle` and `isValidHandle` covering:
- Persian, Arabic, Japanese, Chinese, Korean, Russian scripts
- Special character removal (apostrophes, punctuation)
- Uppercase/lowercase handling (backward compatible)
- Empty handle fallback

✅ **Uppercase Latin handles fixed** - Added `.toLowerCase()` before validation to maintain backward compatibility

✅ **Special characters in kebabCase** - Kept `toHandle` function (not replaced with kebabCase) but improved it to handle non-latic characters while still removing special chars like apostrophes

✅ **Trailing newlines added** - Fixed formatting in changeset and validate-handle files

So now:
- ✅ `toHandle` is preserved (backward compatible)
- ✅ `toHandle` now properly handles Persian/Arabic/Japanese/etc. characters
- ✅ `toHandle` still removes special characters (apostrophes, `!@#$%`, etc.)
- ✅ `isValidHandle` is Unicode-aware with backward compatible lowercase normalization

Thank you for your contribution, @Cpidar\!

The formatting issue from the last review is resolved — Prettier no longer flags the blank line after the opening `{` in `to-handle.ts` and `validate-handle.ts`. 👍

While re-reviewing the Unicode handling, I found a correctness gap that should be addressed before we move forward.

**Required changes:**
- [ ] Align the character classes in `toHandle` and `isValidHandle` so that every handle `toHandle` produces is accepted by `isValidHandle` — see Potential Bugs below.

**Potential Bugs:**

⚠️ **`packages/core/utils/src/common/to-handle.ts` / `validate-handle.ts`** — `toHandle` can produce handles that `isValidHandle` rejects, re-introducing the exact error this PR fixes (for common Japanese titles).

`toHandle` keeps any character in `\p{L}`:
```typescript
.replace(/[^\p{L}\p{N}\s_-]/gu, "")
```
but `isValidHandle` only accepts `\p{Ll}` + `\p{Lo}` + `\p{N}`:
```typescript
return /^[\p{Ll}\p{Lo}\p{N}]+(?:-[\p{Ll}\p{Lo}\p{N}]+)*$/u.test(value)
```

`\p{L}` also includes **modifier letters** (`\p{Lm}`), which `\p{Ll}`/`\p{Lo}` do not. Two very common Japanese characters fall into `\p{Lm}`:
- `ー` (U+30FC, prolonged sound mark) — used in loanwords like `ラーメン`, `コーヒー`, `サーバー`
- `々` (U+3005, iteration mark) — used in `様々`, `人々`, `時々`

So `toHandle("ラーメン")` returns `"ラーメン"` (the `ー` is preserved), but `isValidHandle("ラーメン")` returns `false`.

This matters because auto-generated handles are validated. In `product-module-service.ts` → `createProducts_`, `normalizeCreateProductInput` sets `productData.handle = toHandle(productData.title)` first, then `validateProductCreatePayload` → `validateProductPayload` runs `isValidHandle(productData.handle)`. Creating a product titled `ラーメン` therefore still throws:

```
Invalid product handle 'ラーメン'. It must contain URL safe characters
```

which is the very failure mode this PR is meant to fix for non-Latin titles.

Suggested fix: make the two functions agree on the allowed set. The simplest option is to include modifier letters in the validation class:
```typescript
return /^[\p{Ll}\p{Lo}\p{Lm}\p{N}]+(?:-[\p{Ll}\p{Lo}\p{Lm}\p{N}]+)*$/u.test(value)
```
(Alternatively, strip `\p{Lm}` in `toHandle` instead — but preserving these characters is more correct for Japanese/Chinese.) Please also add a test case covering this (e.g. `ラーメン` and `様々`) and assert the invariant `isValidHandle(toHandle(title)) === true` so the two stay in sync.

Everything else from prior reviews remains resolved (changeset format, comprehensive Unicode tests, uppercase ASCII rejection, double quotes, trailing commas/newlines, accurate JSDoc).

commit_history.message:
fix(product): Support non-Latin characters in product handles with Unicode validation

PROBLEM:
Products with non-Latin titles (Persian, Arabic, Japanese, Chinese, Korean,
Russian, etc.) cannot be created because auto-generated handles fail validation:
"Invalid product handle '-'. It must contain URL safe characters"

Root cause analysis revealed inconsistency in the codebase:
- Products use `toHandle()` → strips non-ASCII characters → empty/partial handle
- Categories use `kebabCase()` → preserves Unicode characters → works correctly
- Collections use `kebabCase()` → preserves Unicode characters → works correctly

SOLUTION:
1. Replace `toHandle(title)` with `kebabCase(title)` in product creation
   - Aligns products with categories and collections behavior
   - Uses existing, tested slugification logic

2. Update `isValidHandle()` to support Unicode letters
   - New regex: `/^[\p{L}\p{N}]+(?:-[\p{L}\p{N}]+)*$/u`
   - Allows any letter from any language while maintaining security
   - Still rejects spaces, special characters, leading/trailing hyphens

3. Remove unused `toHandle` import from product module

IMPACT:
- ✅ Persian: "کتاب-فارسی" → valid
- ✅ Arabic: "الكتاب-العربي" → valid
- ✅ Japanese: "私の-製品" → valid
- ✅ Chinese: "我的-产品" → valid
- ✅ Korean: "나의-제품" → valid
- ✅ Russian: "мой-продукт" → valid
- ✅ English: "my-product" → valid (backward compatible)
- ❌ "my product" → invalid (space)
- ❌ "product@" → invalid (special char)

INDUSTRY STANDARD:
This approach mirrors WordPress/WooCommerce which support UTF-8 in slugs
rather than forcing Latin-only characters. Modern ecommerce platforms
recognize that URLs can safely contain Unicode characters.

Closes #14378

fix(product): Restore toHandle function for product handle generation
The previous change replaced toHandle with kebabCase, which caused
regressions with special characters (apostrophes, punctuation).

Now toHandle has been improved to handle Persian/Arabic/Japanese/etc.
while still removing special characters. Keeping toHandle ensures
backward compatibility and proper sanitization."

commit_history.message:
fix(utils): Address PR review feedback and improve the functionality of toHandle and isValidHandle

- Replace single quotes with double quotes in replace() calls
- Update JSDoc comments to match new implementation
- Add explicit check for uppercase ASCII letters (A-Z)
- Remove .toLowerCase() to maintain consistency with auto-generated handles
- Update regex to use \p{Ll}\p{Lo} instead of \p{L} for precision
- Add test for uppercase rejection to prevent case-sensitive duplicate issues
- Update JSDoc examples to show uppercase rejection behavior
- Generate random fallback handles (e.g., 'product-abc123') instead of empty strings. This ensures every product gets a valid, unique handle and prevents
database constraint violations."
- Update toHandle tests to expect fallback behavior

commit_history.message:
fix(utils): Include modifier letters (\\p{Lm}) in isValidHandle

Japanese prolonged sound mark (ー) and iteration mark (々) are in the
\\p{Lm} (modifier letter) Unicode category.

- toHandle preserves these characters (\\p{L} includes \\p{Lm})
- isValidHandle previously rejected them (only \\p{Ll} + \\p{Lo})

This caused auto-generated handles for Japanese titles like 'ラーメン'
to fail validation.

Changes:
- Add \\p{Lm} to isValidHandle regex
- Add invariant test ensuring isValidHandle(toHandle(title)) === true
- Add Japanese test cases for ー and 々

Now common Japanese words work correctly.
